relationship_to_restored_text: Interpretive contemplative layer aligned by verse. This does not replace the source-audited restored translation.

verses.mystical_translation: David's Hebron household begins with Amnon and Daniel, each named through a mother.
Absalom and Adonijah enter the line through Maacah and Haggith.
Shephatiah and Ithream complete the six sons born in Hebron.
The family list is joined to years of rule, binding household and throne together.
Bathsheba's four sons are named, though the list does not tell the violence that preceded Solomon's birth.
More sons of Jerusalem are remembered.
Nogah, Nepheg, and Japhia remain within the royal household.
Three more names complete the Jerusalem sons.
Concubines remain unnamed, while Tamar is named as sister and survivor beyond the list's silence.
The royal line moves from Solomon toward Rehoboam, Abijah, Asa, and Jehoshaphat.
Joram, Ahaziah, and Joash continue the succession.
Amaziah, Uzziah, and Jotham follow.
Ahaz, Hezekiah, and Manasseh carry the throne through conflicting legacies.
Amon and Josiah close this sequence.
Josiah's sons stand at the edge of national collapse.
Jehoiakim's line moves toward Jeconiah and Zedekiah under imperial pressure.
Jeconiah is remembered not only as king but as captive.
His household continues inside exile.
Zerubbabel, Shimei, Meshullam, Hananiah, and Shelomith carry postexilic memory.
Five more descendants preserve the fragile continuation of the house.
The line branches through names whose exact relationships are textually uncertain.
Shemaiah's household continues despite the archive's difficult counting.
Neariah's three sons are remembered.
Seven sons of Elioenai close the genealogy without closing the people's future.

contemplative_note: Royal genealogy can make power look smooth. The surrounding stories reveal rape, murder, rivalry, exile, captivity, and mothers carrying dynastic consequences. The contemplative task is to remember the people flattened by succession lists—especially Bathsheba, Tamar, unnamed concubines, and families living after empire breaks the throne.
